question: A Type B (flat) tympanogram with no compliance peak, in a child with conductive hearing loss and a recent upper respiratory tract infection, is most consistent with otitis media with effusion (glue ear).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Type B = flat trace = no middle ear compliance = fluid or mass in the middle ear. In a child with CHL and post-URTI, Type B tympanogram = OME (glue ear) until proven otherwise. Type C (peak shifted to negative pressure) = Eustachian tube dysfunction without effusion. Type A = normal.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A Type B tympanogram is the classic impedance finding in otitis media with effusion (OME). Fluid in the middle ear eliminates the pressure-compliance relationship, producing a flat trace with no peak. Combined with the history of a recent URTI in a child and conductive hearing loss on audiometry, this triad confirms OME (glue ear). A Type A trace (normal peak at 0 daPa) would rule this out.
